gen-eater-fs-supreme: Dark and aggressive, Eater lays down thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems, with wide gaps between letters. And Supreme counters with a thick, heavy-looking strip of text, its letters held open rather than curled shut.
gen-flavors-switzer: Switzer leads with a tall waist line and wire-like letterforms. Flavors brings whimsical, towering lowercase and diagonals as hefty as its stems, while Switzer simply stays approachable and Swiss in its tidy, tubular build.
gen-gf-autour-one-work-sans: Expressive, bold, and unashamedly round. Autour One keeps a clear channel leading into each curve, while Work Sans, a modern sans-serif with a high mean line, can take a slightly larger size to lean into that openness.
gen-gf-funnel-display-fs-asap: Commanding in a spaghetti-like way, Funnel Display draws every stroke at a single width with little step down from capitals to lowercase. But Asap is the one built for readability, its c forms opening as plain arcs beside a body height nearly level with the capitals.
gen-gf-grandstander-fs-epilogue: Bold and expressive, Grandstander runs plain constant-width lines with short ascenders and a tall x-height, while Epilogue, a plain sans, adds curvy, wire-like monoline letters. Approachable through and through.
gen-gf-love-ya-like-a-sister-fs-merriwea: Ascenders barely clear the x-height in Love Ya Like A Sister, giving a ruler-straight line with terminal tips pointing outward. Merriweather Sans follows with tall lowercase that makes words look sturdy, its e opening clearly to the right, and the heading earns its keep when big and short.
gen-gf-metamorphous-fs-public-sans: Wide-berthed and high-waisted, Metamorphous mixes fat and slim strokes only softly, with generous sidebearings all around. And Public Sans, a plain sans with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, would read in a trustworthy, steady way over a longer passage.
gen-gf-oxanium-fs-supreme: A high x-height makes Oxanium's lowercase look big, with uninterrupted monoline strokes and curves ending in clear daylight. Supreme, a sans-serif with a thick, heavy-looking strip of text, would read crisp and confident across a longer passage.
gen-gf-paprika-archivo: Commanding and expressive, Paprika scatters its letters at a distance and fills the line with lowercase that looks like capitals. Archivo steps in with outward-opening curves and a firm x-height.
gen-gf-paprika-fs-asap: Readable and professional, Asap draws its c forms as open arcs, with a body height nearly matching the capitals. Paprika's scattered, capital-like lowercase is the pair's boldest quality.
